title: Úthald  v0.6.6 Bunch of bug fixed and some big updates!
author: Rough-Bat4040
selftext:
I've been building Úthald, a graveyard survival game that runs in a browser, mostly with Claude Code. This sub asks for the how rather than the what, so here's the how.

The split is simple. I direct, and I'm the one who says no. Claude writes the code, does the research and runs the measurements. I judge anything that gets seen or heard. Three of the four music tracks it generated were rejects. A blur effect took three failed attempts before the research turned up that I'd been asking for the wrong thing entirely. That ratio is the job, not a sign it's going badly.

The biggest single improvement was making it measure instead of guess.

When the new title music needed to sit at the same volume as the in-game music, it didn't get a hand tuned number. Both tracks got measured to the same loudness figure and matched to two decimal places.

When subtitles needed to line up with singing, nobody eyeballed the timing. It bandpassed the audio down to the frequency range a voice sits in, took the volume envelope, and grouped it into phrases. It found exactly twelve, which is exactly how many sung lines there are, and the caption times came straight out of that.

When the screen edges looked wrong, it raycast the four corners of the view onto the ground to work out how much world the camera can actually see. That turned out to be a bug I'd already blamed on three different lighting effects.

Every one of those swapped an argument about taste for a number.

Second biggest was writing rules the build enforces instead of remembers. The packaging script won't run if the version on the title screen doesn't match the newest patch note. The same check caught a debug page and four unused audio files about to ship to players. A rule nothing enforces is a rule you skip on the one busy day it matters.

Tools, plainly. three.js and pmndrs/postprocessing for the game, Claude Code for the code and the research, ElevenLabs for sound effects, ambience and music, image generation for the painted night sky and the carved stone lettering, and ffmpeg for anything audio that needed measuring rather than listening to. Every character, weapon and gravestone is CC0 work by Kay Lousberg, Kenney and Quaternius, who are human artists, and the game wouldn't look like this without them.

There's also a written ledger of every session and a separate player facing changelog, because the developer record and the player record are different documents, and writing one into the other loses both.

Free, browser, still very much an alpha: [https://windigo2.itch.io/uthald](https://windigo2.itch.io/uthald)
